provenance.text: When using this factory (via "loop.set_task_factory(asyncio.eager_task_factory)"), coroutines begin execution synchronously during "Task" construction. Tasks are only scheduled on the event loop if they block. This can be a performance improvement as the overhead of loop scheduling is avoided for coroutines that complete synchronously.
provenance.title: asyncio-task

provenance.text: An optional keyword-only *context* argument allows specifying a custom "contextvars.Context" for the *coro* to run in. If no *context* is provided, the Task copies the current context and later runs its coroutine in the copied context.
provenance.title: asyncio-task

provenance.text: If set to "True" and the event loop is running, the task will start executing the coroutine immediately, until the first time the coroutine blocks.
provenance.title: asyncio-task

provenance.text: If the coroutine returns or raises without blocking, the task will be finished eagerly and will skip scheduling to the event loop.

provenance.text: The first statement in the coroutine "main()" creates "task_b" and schedules it for execution via the event loop. Then, "coro_a()" is repeatedly awaited. Control never cedes to the event loop, which is why we see the output of all three "coro_a()" invocations before "coro_b()"'s output:
provenance.title: a-conceptual-overview-of-asyncio

provenance.text: If we change "await coro_a()" to "await asyncio.create_task(coro_a())", the behavior changes. The coroutine "main()" cedes control to the event loop with that statement. The event loop then proceeds through its backlog of work, calling "task_b" and then the task which wraps "coro_a()" before resuming the coroutine "main()".
provenance.title: a-conceptual-overview-of-asyncio

provenance.text: Immediate execution of the coroutine is a semantic change. If the coroutine returns or raises, the task is never scheduled to the event loop. If the coroutine execution blocks, the task is scheduled to the event loop. This change may introduce behavior changes to existing applications. For example, the application's task execution order is likely to change.
provenance.title: asyncio-task
